scenes.desc: El grunge, revival del hard rock de los setenta y renacimiento musical de Seattle, fue uno de los grandes fenómenos de los noventa (casi solo en EE UU). Green River lo inauguran (Come On Down) y Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Melvins y Mudhoney fijan sus cuatro puntos cardinales; Nirvana, con Nevermind, lo convierten en una tragaperras y en la banda sonora de la crisis nerviosa de una generación. Después, Alice In Chains (Dirt), Foo Fighters, Hammerbox, GodHeadSilo, Everclear, Stone Temple Pilots, Tool (el grupo más innovador de la segunda generación: Aenima, Lateralus), God Machine, Helmet, Quicksand, Urge Overkill, los Smashing Pumpkins (Siamese Dream, Mellon Collie), Scarce, Creed, Bush, Manic Street Preachers, Silverchair.

podcast.title: Restored 1965 Ford Falcon Van
podcast.body: Despite his rock star status, Dave Grohl's all-time favorite vehicle is a 1965 Ford Falcon van. He discovered the van in the Arizona desert with three flat tires, purchased it, and had it customized by King T's Customs in California. The original 85 horsepower inline 6 engine was replaced with a new V8, and the entire vehicle was restored and customized. "He likes his gunmetal grey 2002 BMW M5, but his all-time favorite is a 1965 Ford Falcon van."

podcast.title: Dave Grohl Solo Cassette "Pocket Watch" (1990) – Under the Name "Late"
podcast.body: Before joining Nirvana and years before the Foo Fighters, Dave Grohl released a cassette-only recording at the very end of 1990 under the name "Late," recording songs with his friend Barnett Jones. The tape is called *Pocket Watch* and includes "Just Another Story About Skeater Thompson," written about the bassist whose romantic troubles indirectly led Grohl to Nirvana. "The only place it can be found is on a cassette only release that Dave released under the name Late."

podcast.title: John Silva's Continuous Management (Since 1995)
podcast.body: When the Foo Fighters began in 1995, following the end of Nirvana in 1994, John Silva was there for Dave Grohl and has remained his manager through all subsequent developments. Silva, heading Silver Artist Management, navigates Grohl's diverse ideas, including books, documentaries, and various tour concepts, ensuring they come to fruition.

podcast.title: Taylor Hawkins Joins the Band (1997)
podcast.body: On March 18, 1997, it was officially announced that Taylor Hawkins was joining the Foo Fighters. He transitioned from being the drummer for Alanis Morissette, who at the time was a bigger act, to an up-and-coming rock band featuring the former Nirvana drummer, Dave Grohl. "So on March 18th, 1997, it was announced that Taylor was officially a food fighter."

Read each item carefully, and on separate paper note any objections, questions, or impossibilities as they relate to your situation by category." It included sections on billing, insurance, interviews, licenses, production requirements (power, lighting, security), dressing rooms, and crew catering. "to save time and to be totally clear, do not amend or change this rider for return."

podcast.title: "Dave of Thrones" Tour (2015)
podcast.body: After Dave Grohl's severe leg injury in Gothenburg, Sweden, the Foo Fighters returned to touring later that summer with Grohl performing from a specially constructed "Dave of Thrones." This elaborate, over-the-top throne was made of guitar necks and equipped with lights, allowing Grohl to continue playing while recovering from surgery. "The food fighters did return to the stage later that summer with Dave sitting in his Dave of Thrones, a special over-the-top throne made of guitar necks and equipped with lights."

podcast.body: Following Taylor Hawkins' death on March 25, 2022, the Foo Fighters canceled all their scheduled shows for the remainder of the year. This decision reflected a period of healing, grieving, and reorganizing for the band, leaving their future uncertain. "The Fufighters have canceled all their shows for the rest of 2022."

podcast.title: Taylor Hawkins' Death (March 25, 2022)
podcast.body: Foo Fighters drummer Taylor Hawkins died suddenly on March 25, 2022, in Bogota, Colombia, just before the band was set to headline a festival. At approximately 7:40 PM on that Friday night, a call was made from a Four Seasons property reporting a guest with severe chest pains, but EMS responders arrived too late. Officially, he died from complications related to an enlarged heart (cardiomegaly), which weighed 600 grams (compared to a normal 300 grams). Although his doctors were aware of his enlarged heart for years, attributing it to his active lifestyle of surfing, biking, and intense drumming, little other information regarding his death was released, due to an "airtight" news blackout imposed by the band and management. This lack of information fueled conspiracy theories, though sources suggested a congenital problem exacerbated by exhaustion, as Hawkins had reportedly been feeling "rough" in the months leading up to the South American tour. His death profoundly impacted Dave Grohl, the Foo Fighters, and millions of fans globally. "Taylor was dead. Officially, he died of complications involving an enlarged heart, something called cardiomagalley."

podcast.title: 606 Studios: The All-Purpose Hub (Northridge, California)
podcast.body: In 2005, following the success of the "One by One" album, the Foo Fighters invested $750,000 to establish their 8,000-square-foot 606 Studios (also known as 606 West) in Northridge, California. Dave Grohl describes it as the "all-purpose Foo Fighters hub" where they rehearse, store gear, record albums, and host press events. The studio, originally a warehouse and once the home of a woman being stalked, was inspired by ABBA's Polar Studios and prominently features the recording console from the legendary Sound City Studios, used by Nirvana, Red Hot Chili Peppers, Rage Against the Machine, Slipknot, and Tom Petty. "By the time the Fuzc got to the one by one album in 2005, they had enough money to invest in their own recording studio in Northridge, California. They call it 606 Studios."

"And then there was the time she accused Dave of hitting on Francis, Kurt and Courtney's daughter."

podcast.body: The band is noted for the immense joy and fun they visibly exude during their live performances. The interviewer observed that there has never been a time when the band didn't appear to be having more fun than anyone should be allowed. "there are five guys on stage having more fun than anybody should ever be allowed to have."

"Besides, the food fighters are not only a big band, but a massive corporation on which many people depend on for their livelihoods. podcast.title: Cancelled Abu Dhabi Gig Due to Medical Emergency
podcast.body: In December 2021, the Foo Fighters cancelled a scheduled gig after the Formula One race in Abu Dhabi because a band member (later suggested to be Taylor) had a medical emergency requiring transfer to a Chicago hospital while awaiting a commercial flight. "And now let's go back to December 2021. The food fighters were scheduled to play a gig after the final Formula One race in Abu Dhabi. But they never made it. We heard much later that a member of the band had a medical emergency and had to be transferred to the hospital in Chicago where the band was scheduled to take a commercial flight to the Middle East. That band member apparently was Taylor."

podcast.title: Commercial Success
podcast.body: Since their debut, Foo Fighters have released nine studio albums, selling around 13 million copies in the US and a similar amount worldwide. They have won four Grammy Awards and performed for tens of millions of people globally. "In the quarter century since the dissolution of Nirvana, there have been nine Foo Fighters studio albums, something about 13 million copies in the US alone, and about the same amount worldwide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Commitment to 100% Live Performance
podcast.body: The Foo Fighters are known for their unwavering commitment to performing "100% live" on stage. During a June 2024 concert at London Stadium, they humorously dubbed their tour "the Errors Tour," stating, "We've had more than a few eras and even more than a few effing errors. That's because we actually play live," contrasting their authentic, live-error-prone approach with artists who use pre-recorded elements. "When the food fighters step on stage, they are 100% live."

podcast.body: This established band continued its characteristic musical output throughout the 2010s, contrasting with the softer pop alt-rock trend, and experienced crossover airplay on active rock radio stations. podcast.body: Foo Fighters are one of the acts from the 90s that continued to be very popular, making it difficult for new artists to break through in the 21st century due to their continued demand and airplay.

podcast.title: Continuing Public Criticism and Apology
podcast.body: Courtney Love has repeatedly called Dave Grohl's reputation as "the nicest guy in rock" a "sham." In the summer of 2021, she posted an "incendiary" message about Dave Grohl and Trent Reznor on Instagram. This post was later deleted, followed by an apology where she acknowledged being "insensitive and it was wrong" and committed to being more responsible with her words. Dave Grohl and Trent Reznor have maintained silence on these incidents. "Courtney has said several times that Dave's reputation is the nicest guy in rock is a sham."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dave Grohl Leg Break Faked Theory
podcast.body: Despite Dave Grohl breaking his leg in Guttenberg, Sweden in June 2015 and finishing the show, some people claim the injury was faked. They argue that everything, from the canceled shows to the publicly available X-rays, was a ruse to allow the band to return triumphantly with Grohl's famous throne and sell commemorative t-shirts, even though the tour, including a Wembley Stadium show, was already sold out. "They claim that this was all faked. Everything from the canceled shows to the X-rays that were made available to the public."

podcast.title: Dave Grohl and Taylor Hawkins' Close Friendship
podcast.body: Dave Grohl and Taylor Hawkins shared an exceptionally close bond, described as "brothers from another mother," with Dave stating he'd "take a bullet for Taylor." Their friendship was essential to keeping Dave grounded and played a significant role in the overall well-being and dynamics of the band. "Second, Taylor was Dave's best friend in the whole world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dave Grohl's Concern for Taylor Hawkins
podcast.body: Following Taylor Hawkins' past heroin overdose and near-fatal coma, Foo Fighters frontman Dave Grohl was highly protective of him, determined not to lose another bandmate to drug-related causes, having already experienced the death of Kurt Cobain. This suggests Grohl maintained a vigilant watch over Hawkins' well-being. "His best buddy, Dave Grohl, wasn't about to lose him on his watch. He'd already been through that with Kurt."

podcast.body: Dave Grohl directed the "Sound City" documentary and was involved in the "Sonic Highways" HBO series. podcast.body: Dave Grohl, Taylor Hawkins's best friend, was deeply committed to preventing Taylor from relapsing into careless drug use, especially given Grohl's own past experiences with loss. "And Dave Grohl, his best friend of the whole world, had been through enough hurt in his life. There was no way he was going to let his brother from another mother go down that route."

podcast.title: Dave Grohl's Songwriting Method for Sonic Highways
podcast.body: For the "Sonic Highways" album, Dave Grohl developed a unique songwriting technique. After spending a week in each city talking with local musicians and absorbing the environment, he would compile a transcription of these conversations. He then cut and pasted words and phrases from these interviews to form the lyrics for that city's song. "Dave would sit down with a transcription of the conversations he'd had. And then sort of cut and paste words and phrases from those conversations and interviews into what would become the lyrics for that city's song."

podcast.body: Dave Roll has been giving numerous interviews and performing on tour, singing extensively, and is very pleased with the outcome of the *Concret and Gold* album, especially its production quality. "el está muy contento con el resultado, sobre todo con la producción."

podcast.body: The Foo Fighters released a disco tribute album, "Hail Satin," under the alter ego The Dee Gees, on Record Store Day 2021, covering Bee Gees and Andy Gibb songs as a loving homage rather than a parody. "This is not a parody or something that the Foo Fighters did to make fun of the Bee Gees. It is done out of love for the Bee Gees and disco."

podcast.title: Urine Test Findings and OD Dismissal
podcast.body: A urine test after Taylor Hawkins's death revealed traces of opioids, antidepressants, anti-anxiety medications, and THC, but the speaker dismisses the theory of an overdose due to the nature of a urine test (not blood), unknown concentrations/combinations, and potential for common substances like codeine in cough syrup or lingering THC. And yes, a urine test after he died revealed traces of opioids and he depressants anti-anxiety medications in THC. But that was a urine test, not a blood test. And we don't know the exact concentrations or combinations of those drugs. So to say that he died from an OD is jumping to conclusions."

xref.body: In October 1994, Dave Grohl booked six days of studio time in Seattle with Barrett Jones to record demos, playing all instruments himself. His sole purpose for these sessions was to "prove to himself that he could do it, that he could still make music," without any intention of pursuing a record contract. He would record his drum parts, then move to the control room for guitar, and then other instruments, completing each song in approximately 40 to 45 minutes. "His only purpose, his sole purpose was to prove to himself that he could do it, that he could still make music."

xref.title: Retaining Music Ownership via Roswell Records (1994)
xref.body: After his Pre-Foo Fighters demos were bootlegged and he was "bestieged with offers," Dave Grohl decided to protect his interests by setting up his own record company, Roswell Records. This was a direct result of his experience with the royalty issues in Nirvana, and his determination to "retain ownership of his music." He informed potential business partners that they would "have to go through" his label. "Dave was determined to retain ownership of his music."

xref.title: "Foo Fighters" Name Origin and Dislike
xref.body: Dave Grohl chose the name "Foo Fighters" for his project after a term used by World War II pilots to describe mysterious "balls of fire over Allied lines" (UFOs). The French word "feu" (fire) influenced the term. He preferred a cloaked, anonymous name, wanting people to think it was a band even though there wasn't one at the time. Despite the name's origins, Dave Grohl "thinks the name Foo Fighters is dumb" and feels "stuck with the name" because the project unexpectedly succeeded. "The most charming thing I saw were the throw pillows on the couches. They were made by Dave's mum from his old concert t-shirts."

xref.title: Neil Peart's Drumming Influence
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins credits Neil Peart's drumming from Rush records for influencing "any crazy fill" he performs on the drums. This highlights Peart's lasting impact on Hawkins' percussive style within the Foo Fighters. "A lot of like anything weird that I do on the drums is usually ripped off from a rush record, like any crazy fill."

xref.title: Post-Nirvana Leadership – Foo Fighters
xref.body: Following the death of Kurt Cobain, Dave Grohl surprised many by stepping out from behind the drum kit. He transitioned to the role of leader, singer, and guitarist for his new band, the Foo Fighters, demonstrating his skills as a musician, songwriter, and singer that many had not expected. "After Kurt's death Dave stepped up from behind the kid as the leader singer and guitarist of the foo fighters."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Precedent for Band Disbanding After Drummer's Death
xref.body: Led Zeppelin's decision to disband after John Bonham's death on September 25, 1980, serves as a significant precedent for the Foo Fighters' situation after Taylor Hawkins' passing. The band determined that "without Bonzo, there was no Led Zeppelin," and consequently folded. "When John Bonham died on September 25, 1980, there was no question that the band was done."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Preferred Guitar for Foo Fighters Recordings
xref.body: Dave Grohl's absolute favorite guitar is a 1967 ES-335. This particular instrument has been exclusively used to record every single guitar part on every Foo Fighters song ever produced. "His absolute favorite guitar is a 1967 ES-335. It's been used to track every single guitar part on every single Fufiter song ever recorded."

xref.title: Producer for Pixies and Foo Fighters
xref.body: Gil Norton is a producer known for his work with bands like the Pixies and the Foo Fighters. He was considered to produce Sum 41's "Screaming Bloody Murder" album, but his unavailability led Derek Whibley to produce it himself. "Gil Norton, a guy known for his work with the Pixies and the Who Fighters, couldn't do it."

xref.title: Recognition of Luck and Hard Work
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins acknowledged that his successful career in the Foo Fighters was a combination of both luck and hard work. He was humble about his achievements, understanding that hard work alone doesn't guarantee success in the music industry. "if you get lucky like me, you may make a really good living."

xref.title: Recruitment of Sunny Day Real Estate Rhythm Section
xref.body: Dave Grohl recruited the entire rhythm section from the band Sunny Day Real Estate, who then became a significant part of the Foo Fighters' lineup. "decided that they'd rather work for Dave Grohl and became one half of the food fighters."

xref.title: Rivers Cuomo Identical Theory
xref.body: A theory, which originated on Reddit, claims that Kurt Cobain and Rivers Cuomo of Weezer are the same person, suggesting Kurt did not die. Proponents point to a November 1998 "Goat Punishment" secret show where Weezer played six Nirvana songs, the shared biographer John D. Luerssen, the fact that both bands were signed to the same label, and Weezer having toured with the Foo Fighters. The theory also notes that Nirvana and Weezer's studio and tour dates never conflicted. "The first is that Kurt and River's Cuomo of Weezer are actually the same person."

xref.title: Robert Lang Studios Preference
xref.body: Robert Lang Studios, located north of Seattle, was a favorite recording spot for Alice in Chains. This studio also holds significance for the Foo Fighters, as it was where their first record was made and where Nirvana recorded their last completed song. "Robert Lang Studios, a place north of the city that was a favorite spot for Alice and Chains."

xref.title: Speculated Post-Nirvana Life (if Kurt Lived)
xref.body: It is speculated that Dave Grohl, freed from being Kurt's timekeeper, would have continued with Foo Fighters, with little change to his trajectory. "Dave Grohl finally freed from being just Kurt's timekeeper would have gone about his merry way with the food fighters. I can't see that being much different."

xref.body: Them Crooked Vultures was formed as a supergroup, bringing together Josh Homme, Foo Fighters' Dave Grohl, and Led Zeppelin's bass player John Paul Jones. "Josh was one-third of them crooked vultures, a supergroup that featured Buddy Dave Grohl and Led Zeppelin bass player John Paul Jones."

xref.body: The band formed after years of casual discussions among Dave Grohl (Foo Fighters), Josh Homme (Queens of the Stone Age), and John Paul Jones (Led Zeppelin) about creating music together. They finally decided to make it a reality. "After years of joking about forming a band together, Dave Grohl of the Fung Fighters, Josh Hommie of Queens of the Stone Age, and Led Zeppelin's John Paul Jones decided to make it happen with them crooked vultures."

xref.title: Survival of Late Songs
xref.body: Over the years, though, songs from Dave Grohl's Late project have surfaced in various forms. In addition to bootlegs, tracks have appeared on 7-inch compilations, and some were re-recorded and renamed for Foo Fighters releases, demonstrating the enduring influence of his early solo work. "Over the years, though, songs from late have shown up. In addition to the bootlegs, tracks have appeared on 7-inch compilations, somewhere we recorded, and renamed for Foo Fighters releases."

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' All-Time Favorite Band
xref.body: Queen held a special place as Taylor Hawkins' all-time favorite band. He greatly admired their music and often dared to tackle Freddie Mercury's vocal parts when he would step out from behind the drum kit to sing for the Foo Fighters. "Queen was his all time favorite band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' Favorite Drummer Ever
xref.body: Roger Taylor was Taylor Hawkins' favorite drummer of all time. This admiration was evident from Hawkins' enthusiastic reaction to a poster of Taylor's solo album "Fun in Space" at the Foo Fighters' studio. "That's Roger Taylor, man. He's my favorite drummer ever."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Temporary Departure and QOTSA Drumming
xref.body: After Taylor Hawkins's near-fatal overdose in 2001, Dave Grohl stepped away from the Foo Fighters to "sort his head out." During this period, he briefly became the drummer for Queens of the Stone Age. "That's when he briefly became drummer for Queens of the Stone Age."

xref.title: The Wallflowers' Consistency
xref.body: Jacob Dylan has been the sole consistent member of The Wallflowers throughout its existence, a band that remains active today. The lineup has seen several changes, with notable past members including Jack Irons, formerly of the Red Hot Chili Peppers and Pearl Jam, and Rami Jaffee, keyboardist for Foo Fighters. "Jacob has been the only consistent member of The Wallflowers over all these years, which by the way is still a going concern. People to cycle through the band have included former chili peppers and pro jam drummer Jack Irons and Foo Fighters keyboardist Rami Jaffee."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: UFO and Science Fiction Fascination
xref.body: Dave Grohl has had a lifelong fascination with UFOs and science fiction, dating back to his childhood. He would lie in his front yard waiting for UFOs, had "crazy UFO dreams," and loved science fiction toys and action figures. This interest influenced his choice of the name "Foo Fighters" for his band and "Roswell Records" for his label, both referencing UFO phenomena. "Well, for a long time, since I was a kid, I'd always been really fascinated with UFOs."

This situation highlights the ongoing debate within the music industry and among fans regarding the balance between production spectacle and authentic live musicianship. "Remember when they poke fun at Taylor Swift for using pre-recorded bits and her shows?"
